result.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
result.summary: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) requires a method that can understand, generate, reason, and act across diverse domains and modalities. Rather than relying on a single model to master every capability, a promising path toward AGI now is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies (candidates) into a unified AI system. At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost? In this work, we present Route Anything, a unified framework for studying model and policy routing across general-purpose AI systems. We develop a unified theoretical foundation that characterizes optimal routing under quality--cost trade-offs and establishes how the information available to a router determines its attainable performance. To systematically investigate routing across diverse capabilities, we first construct an omni-modal trajectory matrix spanning 25 benchmarks across language understanding, image, video, and speech generation, coding and workplace agents, and robotic manipulation, comprising 374,401 scored runs from 452 candidate configurations. Building on this framework, we train and test different routers to investigate the potential of omni-modal model routing, the capabilities of learned routers, and the conditions under which routing improves efficiency. Our results reveal substantial opportunities for capability orchestration: per-input oracle routing outperforms the best fixed candidate by 5.4 points, and learned routers outperform it by 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, by 2.1 points on video generation, and by 1.1 points on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time. More importantly, routing raises efficiency by 8.82x on average compared with the reference model.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Route Anything 统一框架，研究通用 AI 系统中按任务动态选择模型、工具与策略的路由问题，给出质量—成本权衡下最优路由及「路由器可获信息决定可达性能」的理论刻画，并构建覆盖 25 个基准、452 个候选配置、约 37 万次评分运行的 omni-modal 轨迹矩阵来训练和评测各类路由器。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「可获信息限制路由可达性能」与质量—成本权衡的分析，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的停止决策、动态计算分配及其评价方式提供类比线索，但论文不涉及内部 latent 推理状态，仅供概念核查。
